_comment: CASE 2B -- PARTIAL PARTICIPATION, MILP (single-path) leg. Same shared-NIC topology, same active set [0, 2, 3, 5], same clock and same objective as mini_2gpu_1nic_alltoall_partial_2B.json, solved with the chunk-level MILP (formulation 1) at num_chunks 1: each (src, dst) pair owns exactly ONE indivisible 1 GB chunk that traverses exactly ONE path end to end. Because the solver still picks the BEST single-path assignment, LP-minus-MILP is a LOWER bound on what per-pair multipath is worth.
_known_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION, ACCEPTED -- MILP timing on a non-uniform-bandwidth topology at a sub-chunk epoch. This topology mixes 100Gbps host ports with 50Gbps leaf-spine uplinks, and this file's pinned 0.08 s epoch is SHORTER than one chunk on the 50Gbps link (6.25 GB/s x 0.08 s = 0.5 GB against a 1 GB chunk), so get_beta_num_back returns beta = 1 there. In that regime the MILP's cut-through accounting under-charges TIME: allgather.py pays the store-and-forward cost (1 epoch + beta) ONCE at the first GPU->switch hop and charges every later fabric hop only propagation delay (see the branches at allgather.py switch->switch and the switch->GPU buffer credit), so the delivery epoch it credits is 1 + beta(FIRST hop) instead of the correct 1 + max(beta over the legs used) = ceil(chunk / min bandwidth along the path). CONSEQUENCE: in a MILP schedule from this file, 3-Epochs_Required, 4-Collective_Finish_Time and 5-Algo_Bandwidth are OPTIMISTIC and must not be quoted -- the ROUTING (7-Flows and 8-Chunk paths) is what the file is for, and real timing comes from simulating that routing. Measured on case 1A at this epoch: the MILP reports 0.08 s while every 50Gbps leg on its own chosen path needs 0.16 s to clock the chunk out; the identical run with switch_pipeline false (which does charge the -1 and beta) reports 0.48 s. The LP is NOT affected: continuous flow can be split across epochs, so it has no beta machinery and its per-epoch row (capacity x epoch_duration) is exact -- which is why the fine epoch is kept here rather than coarsened, since it is what makes the LP's makespan exact instead of rounded up. mini_2gpu_2nic (case 3A) is structurally immune: its links are uniform 100Gbps, so one chunk always fits one epoch and beta is 0 everywhere.
_participation: active GPUs [0, 2, 3, 5]; passive GPUs [1, 4, 6, 7]. Node map: 0/1 = srv0.gpu0/gpu1, 2/3 = srv1, 4/5 = srv2, 6/7 = srv3; 8-11 = the rc's; 12/13 = leaf0/leaf1; 14/15 = spine0/spine1. srv0+srv1 on leaf0, srv2+srv3 on leaf1 -- so 3 participants behind leaf0 (one of them a host contributing BOTH GPUs) and 1 behind leaf1, with srv3 fully passive and usable only as a relay. num_chunks 1 = one chunk per (src, dst) PAIR; the chunk axis is widened by the ACTIVE GPU count, giving 12 chunks of 1 GB.
_vs_lp: Differences from mini_2gpu_1nic_alltoall_partial_2B.json, and only these: formulation 1 (MILP) not 2 (LP); symmetry false not true; num_epochs 10 not 12; distinct log_file and schedule_output_file. Held fixed: topo_file, passive_node_indices, chunk_size 1, collective 2, num_chunks 1, switch_copy false, epoch_type 3 / epoch_duration 0.08 (pinned, identical in both), switch_pipeline true, solution_method 1, time_limit 5. ALSO DIFFERENT: objective_type 2 (TOTAL_DEMAND) here against the LP's 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) -- so the difference is integrality PLUS objective, not integrality alone; it is still not granularity. See _objective_note for exactly what that trades.
_objective_note: OBJECTIVE: TOTAL_DEMAND (objective_type 2), NOT the lexicographic 6 the LP partner uses. WHAT IT IS: allgather.py::objective_formulation builds -100 * sum_k max(sum_(s,d,c) total_demand_sat[s][d][c][k] - (Demand - 1), 0). The inner term is 1 exactly when EVERY demand is already satisfied by the end of epoch k and 0 otherwise, so the objective pays 100 per epoch of the horizon that the collective has already finished in -- i.e. it MINIMIZES THE COMPLETION EPOCH directly. That is the point of using it here: '3-Epochs_Required' becomes the quantity the solver is actually optimizing, so a reported makespan can be compared against the analytic bound as a real optimality claim rather than as an artifact of where a latency-sum objective happened to leave the last straggler. WHAT IT GIVES UP -- read this before judging the routing: objective_type 6 carried two lower-priority tiers that 2 does not have. Tier 2 penalized HOST RELAY (volume a GPU forwards on behalf of another GPU) and tier 3 penalized SWITCH-CHAIN LENGTH (flow entering a switch: 0 for a direct link, 1 for gpu->switch->gpu, 3 for a leaf->spine->leaf detour). Under objective 2 the solver is INDIFFERENT among all schedules that finish in the same epoch, so expect gratuitous relays and spine detours that carry no cost -- the schedule stays correct and makespan-optimal, but it is no longer the tidiest routing that achieves that makespan, and a relay or a long chain in the output is no longer evidence that it was needed. MIDDLE GROUND if that matters: objective_type 5 (TOTAL_DEMAND_MIN_SWITCH_HOPS) is this same completion reward plus a GAMMA=1e-4 per-unit penalty on switch->switch flow, small enough never to trade completion time for hops, which restores a shortest-chain preference (but still no relay tier). COST: the objective adds two continuous aux vars and one max_ general constraint per epoch, which is negligible next to the (source, link, chunk, epoch) flow variables. COMPARABILITY CAVEAT: the LP partner still uses objective_type 6, so the LP-vs-MILP difference is no longer integrality ALONE -- it is integrality plus objective. For the makespan that is fine (both are measured against the same analytic lower bound, which neither objective can beat); for a ROUTING diff, remember the LP is tie-broken toward fewer relays and shorter switch chains and this MILP is not.
_why_symmetry_off: Orbit averaging is free on the LP (convex feasible set: the symmetric average of an optimum is an optimum) but a REAL restriction on the integral problem, where an equal split across an orbit need not exist at the integral optimum -- and cutting off that optimum is exactly the measurement error this file exists to avoid.
_expected: WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR IS THE ROUTING, NOT THE CLOCK -- its reported makespan is optimistic at this epoch (see _known_limitation), so take timing from simulation. For reference, the hand-computed single-path answer is still 0.32 s = 4 epochs: srv1's shared NIC must pass 4 chunks at 100Gbps x 0.08 s = 1 chunk per epoch, and that bound does not care about splitting. The cross-leaf chunks are where integrality shows: each must ride ONE 50Gbps uplink and needs 0.16 s = 2 epochs to clock out, against the LP's 0.5/0.5 fan that clears in one. WHAT TO COMPARE: diff the '12-Chunk paths' sections -- every MILP demand should list ONE path, the LP's three cross-leaf demands per direction should be fanned across both spines -- and check that both keep the gpu2<->gpu3 chunks on the NVLink bridge rather than out through the shared NIC, which would push srv1's NIC to 6 chunks and is the most likely way for this instance to come back worse than it should.
_epoch_note: epoch_type 3 (USER_INPUT) with epoch_duration PINNED to 0.08 s = 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, one 100Gbps host port. Deliberately NOT the SLOWEST_LINK value (0.16 s, the 50Gbps uplink) that the full-participation files on this topology use: at 0.16 s the LP's answer is rounded up to the epoch grid, and pinning 0.08 s is what makes the LP's makespan land exactly on its true bound. The price is paid by the MILP leg only, and it is a KNOWN, ACCEPTED inaccuracy in its reported time -- see _known_limitation. Both legs share this clock so the routing comparison stays controlled.
_horizon_note: num_epochs is the MILP's time horizon and it costs (one integer flow variable per source, link, chunk and epoch), so it is kept tight: the binding bound below is 2 epochs and 6 leaves 3x headroom. If the solve comes back INFEASIBLE rather than merely slow, raise this first. With objective_type 2 the horizon no longer DISTORTS the answer, only the model size: the reward is paid per epoch in which the whole collective is already complete, so a larger num_epochs just widens the reward range and the solver still drives the completion epoch down. Contrast objective_type 6, under which the reported makespan was only an upper bound (its tier 1 minimizes the SUM of completion epochs, not the max, so a straggler could drift late inside a generous horizon) -- see _objective_note.
_why_flat_only: hierarchical is false and cannot be true on this topology for either formulation: the host's single external link is the NIC, owned by `rc` rather than by a GPU, so DslTopology._build_cell will not accept these hosts as cells.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. The path is relative to the repo root.
